first_experiment.title: Variance commentary: your way vs Copilot, on made-up numbers

hypothesis.statement: If this user supplies the cause notes, Copilot can produce variance commentary they would send after light edits in at least 30% less time than their usual drafting.
hypothesis.would_be_wrong_if: Assisted drafting takes as long or longer including edits, or needs three or more substantive corrections of causes or numbers.

relevance.why_for_this_user: The pack is this user's largest time block and the commentary is the part they already find slow; a synthetic stand-in keeps within the unclear Copilot data rules.

steps.instruction: Outside close week, copy the layout of one page of your variance table into a new file and fill it with invented numbers. Add 3-4 invented cause notes like the ones ops would tell you. No real figures, names or products.
Write the commentary for that page your usual way. Time it.
Give Copilot the invented table and cause notes; ask for commentary in your pack's style. Edit until you'd send it. Time drafting plus edits.
Compare the two versions and fill the note template: minutes each way, substantive corrections, would-you-send.

materials.description: Invented variance table and cause notes mirroring the real pack's structure.

prediction.user: Maybe 10 minutes saved, but I'll have to rewrite the explanations.
prediction.engine: Expect ≥30% time saving on prose, with corrections concentrated on causal wording and favourable/unfavourable signs.

measures.what: Minutes to finished commentary, usual way
Minutes to sendable commentary with Copilot, including edits
Substantive corrections (wrong cause, wrong number, wrong sign, misleading framing)
Would you send the assisted version after ≤10 minutes of edits?
Where the assisted draft went wrong

learning_criteria.confirms_if: M2 ≤ 0.7 × M1 and M4 = yes and M3 ≤ 2
learning_criteria.informative_note: Either way we learn whether drafting or checking is the real work in the pack.
